original_question: Let α be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action of F2 on a measure space (X, µ), and let e ≠ x be a fixed nonidentity element of F2. Is there a free probability-measure-preserving action β such that Eα = Eβ and x acts ergodically in β?
target_in_paper: Section 13 (Wei Dai), Problem 45(i): given a free, p.m.p., ergodic action alpha of F_2 on (X, mu) and a fixed nonidentity x in F_2, ask whether there is a free, p.m.p. action beta with E_alpha = E_beta and x acting ergodically. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official question very closely: it has the right group F_2, the right hypotheses on alpha (free, p.m.p., ergodic), the right fixed parameter x != e, the right orbit-equivalence requirement E_alpha = E_beta, and the right conclusion that x should act ergodically in beta. It is targeting Problem 45(i), not the separate stronger Miller-Tserunyan question in Problem 45(ii). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: State explicitly that beta is also an action of F_2, not just an unspecified action; this is implicit in Problem 45(i). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Make clear that beta acts on the same space (X, mu); this is implicit once one asks for E_alpha = E_beta as orbit equivalence relations on X. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Define E_alpha and E_beta as the orbit equivalence relations induced by alpha and beta; the paper uses this notation without unpacking it inside Problem 45(i). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Clarify that 'x acts ergodically' means the single measure-preserving transformation beta(x) is ergodic on (X, mu). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Do not strengthen the question by requiring the whole action beta to be ergodic; the paper only asks beta to be free and p.m.p., while demanding ergodicity only for the element x. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let alpha be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action of F_2 on a probability space (X, mu), and fix x in F_2 with x != e. Let E_alpha be the orbit equivalence relation induced by alpha on X, i.e. u E_alpha v iff v = alpha(g)(u) for some g in F_2. Does there exist another free, probability-measure-preserving action beta of F_2 on the same space (X, mu) such that E_beta = E_alpha and the single transformation beta(x) is ergodic? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Section 13, Problem 45(i). Your draft is already almost verbatim to the paper's wording, so the refinement only makes explicit the hidden notation and scope needed to make it fully stand-alone: beta should be an F_2-action on the same space, E_alpha should be identified as the orbit equivalence relation, and 'x acts ergodically' should be read as ergodicity of beta(x). I did not replace it by Problem 45(ii), because the paper presents that as a separate stronger question (credited to Miller-Tserunyan), not as an equivalent reformulation. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
